sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 of the 1905 New Jersey coast volume covers the eastern part of West Ocean Grove and the adjoining edge of Bradley Park, in what is now Neptune Township, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the right of the page. The part runs from 11th Avenue on the south (left) to Pharo Avenue and the north edge, and from Ridge Avenue on the west (top) to Steiner Avenue and Atkins Avenue on the east (bottom). Corlies Avenue crosses the sheet from west to east through the middle, with Division Street parallel to it on the north and 1st Street and Pharo Avenue running north from Division Street. The blocks are lettered West Ocean Grove and Bradley Park, numbered 1 to 7, and laid out in narrow lots, many still vacant. Building is almost entirely frame dwellings with outbuildings. Commercial and institutional buildings are few: the J. S. Hall and F. O. Hurley sale and exchange stables on Ridge Avenue, a blacksmith and wood working shop on Division Street, a dairy and two large greenhouses heated by hot water on the Bradley Park blocks between 11th and Corlies Avenues, and the West Grove M. E. Church at the corner of Corlies and Atkins Avenues. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn in Ridge, 11th, Steiner and Atkins Avenues with hydrants. The area west of 11th Avenue is left blank and marked as sheet 62; neighbouring sheets 43, 44 and 60 are named along the edges.
notes: Steiner Av on this sheet is today part of Atkins Avenue; the modern Steiner Avenue lies further south.
Pharo Av is today Pharo Street.
Corlies Avenue has been widened into a divided road and no longer runs on its 1905 line; its junctions were left out of the fit.
A box at the top right corner names a street cut off by the sheet edge (Myrtl..., probably Myrtle Avenue).
Division Street is drawn 20 ft wide.

map, 60 ft. West Ocean Grove between 11th Av and Atkins/Steiner Av, Ridge Av to the north edge: Corlies Av, Division St, Pharo Av, 1st St. North to the right. Steiner Av here is modern Atkins Avenue; Pharo Av is Pharo Street.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 of the 1905 New Jersey coast volume covers the south-eastern part of West Ocean Grove and Bradley Park in today's Neptune Township, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the right of the page. It runs from Steiner Avenue and Atkins Avenue at the top (west) down to the New York and Long Branch Railroad at the bottom (east), and from 11th Avenue on the south (left) to Bamboo Street and the north edge. Corlies Avenue runs through the middle towards the railroad, with Division Street north of it. The west half is largely open ground: the Bradley Park lots along Steiner Avenue, a large tract crossed by the unopened 12th Avenue (drawn in dashed lines) and enclosed by picket fences, and the Palmateer Bros. lumber, hardware, sash, doors and blinds yard. Along Corlies Avenue stand dwellings, stores, a barber shop, the Unexcelled Fire Dept. No. 2 house with its chemical engine and hose wagon, and the Jacob Stiles express and storage buildings. North of Division Street and around Bamboo Street is a dense quarter of small dwellings, tenements, a colored church, a print shop, a wood working shop, the Russell Hotel and Russell Cottage, Olivet Cottage, Simms Cottage, Simms Villa and the Sea View House. By the railroad are R. E. Thompson's coal pockets and coal, lime and hay yard, a blacksmith, an ice house and a lumber shed. Beyond the tracks, the ground towards S. Main Street belongs to sheets 47 and 55 and is left blank.
notes: Steiner Av on this sheet is today part of Atkins Avenue.
12th Av is drawn as a dashed, unopened street; no modern street follows it.
Bamboo St and the blocks east of Division Street have no surviving streets; Division Street now ends at Atkins Avenue.
Memorial Drive now runs along the railroad across these blocks.
Placed from three points along Atkins Avenue only (one detected, one hand-picked, one carried from sheet 59); low confidence away from that street.

map, 60 ft. Steiner/Atkins Av east to the New York & Long Branch Railroad: 11th Av, unopened 12th Av, Corlies Av, Division St, Bamboo St, Palmateer Bros lumber yard. North to the right. Area east of Division (Bamboo St) has no surviving streets; mask cut at the railroad (S. Main St area belongs to other sheets).

sheet-61-1.description: Main part of sheet 61 of the 1905 New Jersey coast volume, covering the northern edge of Neptune City and the south of Bradley Park, in today's Neptune City and Neptune Township, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the right of the page. It shows the large blocks between Ridge Avenue at the top (west) and Railroad Avenue at the bottom (east), crossed by Steiner Avenue, with 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Avenues running across the page and Evergreen Avenue cutting diagonally between 2nd and 3rd Avenues. The blocks are lettered Neptune City and Bradley Park and are mostly empty, with a few dwellings along 3rd and 4th Avenues. A borough line runs through the blocks between 4th and 5th Avenues. The main buildings are the public school on 3rd Avenue, heated by the Willis warming and ventilating system, the Neptune City Borough Hall and Fire House No. 1 with a double cylinder chemical engine on 2nd Avenue, and the large brick works of Steiner and Co., makers of Universal sleeping garments, on 4th Avenue by Railroad Avenue, with its elevated water tank; the plan notes that admission was refused in March 1905. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches with hydrants are drawn in the avenues. The top left corner of the sheet holds an inset with an enlarged plan of the Mackintosh Toffee Co. (part 2).
notes: Steiner Av here is today Atkins Avenue between 3rd and 5th Avenues; the modern Steiner Avenue continues south of 3rd Avenue.
Railroad Av is today Memorial Drive.
Steiner & Co. works marked 'Admission Refused March '05'.

map, 60 ft. Neptune City and Bradley Park: 2nd to 5th Av between Ridge Av and Railroad Av, Evergreen Av; Steiner & Co. garment works, public school. Two parts: part 1 main map, part 2 inset (enlarged plan of Mackintosh Toffee Co., 7th Av and Railroad Av; also drawn on sheet 62). North to the right.

sheet-61-2.description: Inset on sheet 61 of the 1905 New Jersey coast volume: an enlarged plan of the Mackintosh Toffee Co. works on 7th Avenue at Railroad Avenue in Bradley Park, today in Neptune Township, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the right as on the main sheet. The factory is shown as a long brick building with stock and shipping rooms, candy making rooms, two 75 horsepower boilers and a blower and dynamo room, with a few small outbuildings, at the corner of 7th Avenue and Railroad Avenue. The plan carries the works' fire protection notes: a night watchman with a portable clock and five stations, electric power, coal fuel, electric and gas lights, steam heating by an indirect system, four 1.5 inch vertical pipes with 50 feet of 2 inch hose on each floor, supplied by the Ocean Grove water works, and 72 iron fire pails. A 10 inch water pipe is drawn in 7th Avenue and the tracks of the New York and Long Branch Railroad run along the east side of Railroad Avenue. The same works are drawn at the smaller scale of sheet 62 on block 21, which refers back to this plan.
notes: Railroad Av is today Memorial Drive.
Placed from one junction (7th Avenue / Memorial Drive) with the scale and rotation of the main part of the sheet; low confidence.

map, 60 ft. Neptune City and Bradley Park: 2nd to 5th Av between Ridge Av and Railroad Av, Evergreen Av; Steiner & Co. garment works, public school. Two parts: part 1 main map, part 2 inset (enlarged plan of Mackintosh Toffee Co., 7th Av and Railroad Av; also drawn on sheet 62). North to the right.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 of the 1905 New Jersey coast volume covers Bradley Park, today the part of Neptune Township between Neptune City and West Ocean Grove, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north to the right of the page. It shows a regular grid of long blocks from 5th Avenue on the south (left) to 11th Avenue and Corlies Avenue on the north (right), and from Union Avenue on the west (top) through Stokes Avenue, Ridge Avenue and Steiner Avenue to Railroad Avenue and the New York and Long Branch Railroad on the east (bottom). Logantown Road runs diagonally across the north-west corner to Corlies Avenue. Most blocks are numbered 1 to 24 and divided into numbered lots, nearly all still vacant; dwellings are scattered thinly along Ridge, Stokes and Steiner Avenues and are more frequent towards 10th and 11th Avenues. The Bradley Park Public School, heated by steam and hot air, stands on Ridge Avenue between 9th and 10th Avenues. On block 21 by Railroad Avenue is the Mackintosh Toffee Co., with a reference to the enlarged plan on sheet 61, and by the railroad are the Ocean Grove Water Works catch tanks and a freight house and platform. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches with hydrants are drawn in Ridge, Steiner and several of the avenues.
notes: Stokes Av is today NJ 35 (State Highway 35).
Steiner Av here is today Atkins Avenue.
Railroad Av is today Memorial Drive.
Logantown Road does not survive as a named street.
The 10th Avenue / Ridge Avenue junction lies 6.4 m from the fit and was rejected.

map, 120 ft. Bradley Park: 5th to 11th Av between Union Av and Railroad Av (Stokes, Ridge, Steiner Av), Logantown Road, Corlies Av; Bradley Park Public School, Mackintosh Toffee Co. North to the right.
